description:
You are a hydraulic engineer at a regional flood control district tasked with performing a flood frequency analysis for the White River at Muncie, Indiana for a FEMA flood insurance study update. A terminal is open in the Muncie HEC-RAS project directory.

A USGS peak-flow frequency report has been placed at ~/Documents/usgs_white_river_frequency.txt. This report contains the USGS StreamStats-derived flood frequency estimates (peak discharge in cfs) for return periods of 10, 50, and 100 years at USGS Gauge 03349000 (White River at Muncie, IN).

Your tasks:
1. Read the frequency report to obtain the design peak flows for the 10-year, 50-year, and 100-year return periods.
2. For each return period, modify the upstream boundary condition hydrograph in Muncie.b04 so that its peak flow equals the design peak flow for that return period. Scale all flows in the hydrograph proportionally (the hydrograph shape stays the same; only the magnitude changes). Run the unsteady flow simulation for each scenario and record the resulting overall peak water surface elevation (WSE) in feet.
3. After all three simulations, write the results to ~/Documents/hec_ras_results/frequency_results.csv with columns: return_period,design_flow_cfs,peak_wse_ft (no spaces around commas, one header row, three data rows in ascending return period order).
4. Identify the Base Flood Elevation (BFE), defined as the peak WSE from the 100-year simulation, and write it to ~/Documents/hec_ras_results/bfe_documentation.txt. The file must contain a line in the format: BFE=<value> (e.g. BFE=952.34).

The simulation executable is RasUnsteady and is already in your PATH. After each run, the results are written to Muncie.p04.hdf. Extract peak WSE from the HDF5 results using Python with h5py or the rashdf package. The analysis script ~/Documents/analysis_scripts/analyze_peak_wse.py may be helpful as a reference. Be sure to extract the peak WSE for each scenario before overwriting the HDF5 with the next run.
